_baseline_note: R-MFDN T cell (BERT-base-uncased 110M fine-tuned, mask-weighted mean pool), P2 fold f0, reference-free (i3), visibility-aligned (single visible bit llm_textgen, nkeep=1 so test.mAP == llm AP); BSC $S/runs4f/f0/T_base (5.9 min train, best_val 62.60). Test: ACC 63.45 / AUC 66.86 / mAP 91.60. Context: E004 (order-blind EmbedBagText, 2.1M) gave llm AP 56.81 on the same fold.

factor._note: absent = BERT-base (paper encoder). minitf = MiniTransformerText in encoders.py: E004's 64-d WordPiece table -> Linear 128 + learned positions (max_text_tokens 50), 2 pre-norm transformer encoder layers (4 heads, FFN 256, GELU, dropout 0.1), key-padding from attention_mask, mask-weighted mean, Linear 128->512; 2,299,392 params, from scratch. Same inputs/collate as BERT. Differs from E004 only by word order/context.

hypothesis: Adding word order and token context (2-layer transformer over the same 64-d table, +0.2M params) recovers most of the llm_textgen AP that the order-blind bag lost (E004 56.81): f0 test llm AP >= 90.0 (BERT 91.60), which would show the LLM-script vs ASR-transcript cue is syntactic/contextual but does not require language pretraining; AUC within +-2 of 66.86.
_success_note: test.mAP is exactly llm_textgen AP here (nkeep=1). make_run_report's verdict is strict-sign against BERT; the pre-registered gate is watched.llm_textgen >= 90.0 (equivalence). A result between 56.81 and 90.0 means order helps but pretraining is also needed -> next rung BERT-tiny.

budget._note: E004 trained in 0.8 min; the 2-layer transformer adds negligible compute
